Inspected primary full texts of Sun 2010, Guo 2014, Kauers–Krattenthaler–Müller 2011, and OEIS data do not state the exact uniform 2-adic index shift phase and complete least period for all powers of two. The closest mathematical record entries concern other quantities. Broader general congruence algorithms might encompass derived special cases; no dominating explicit implication was located. Bounded source search and plausible unlocated equivalent literature are recorded as residual risks.

value.rationale: PASS: Least global periods modulo each 2-power are canonical invariants of the central Delannoy sequence, and their exact all-modulus classification is useful independently of the test computations. The uniform leading dyadic shift term gives a sharp index-residue dichotomy and requires a non-obvious cancellation at the first critical valuation a=2; it goes beyond finite tables, general eventual-period existence, or an arbitrary slice.
